title: Score the frozen ORN-to-PN plasticity models once against the sealed day-1 and day-0 wild-type cohorts
status: EXECUTED 2026-09-10 and its primary cohort VOIDED. The Fig3J wild-type arrays are bit-identical to the fit set, so the registered primary holdout was the training data and the artifact's PASSED verdict does not stand. The Fig3H day-0 cohort is genuine and its registered results stand: A1 NO VERDICT on power, A2 PASSED, A3 PASSED. Under the registered verdict rule the experiment returns NO VERDICT.

depends_on.rule: The models scored here are the ones that artifact froze. Their parameters may not be changed, refitted, nudged or reselected, and this contract records their predictions numerically so that the comparison cannot drift.

spent_arrays.why_it_is_spent: opened and scored on 2026-09-09 by stage2-depression-external-test-v1, then used as the fit set by stage2-stp-family-selection-v1

why_this_exists.the_position_before_this_run: ND-06 v0.1, a depression-only rule with parameters taken from a published fit, has faced two independent external tests and passed neither: it over-predicts steady-state depression at 7 Hz by about 16 percentage points, and it fails structurally against wild-type paired-pulse ratios because those exceed one and decrease with interval while a single depleting resource can do neither. Every quantitative dynamical claim this project has made has failed. No tier above V0 is supported.
why_this_exists.what_would_change_that: A model frozen before seeing a cohort, predicting that cohort inside its measurement error, and beating a horizontal line while doing it. That is what this contract scores. It is the first time in this project that a dynamical model has been frozen and then tested rather than inherited and then tested.
why_this_exists.and_what_would_not: A pass here does not make the model right. It is the same laboratory, the same protocol, the same genotype and the same observable as the fit set, differing only in the animals and their age. The acceptance section says exactly what a pass is worth and it is not much more than this: the model generalises across cohorts of the quantity it was fitted to.

primary.cohort: wild type, 1 day post eclosion (24 to 48 h), Orco-GAL4; GH146-QF, QUAS-GFP
primary.why_it_is_the_primary: It is the developmental neighbour of the fit set. The paper reports that eEPSC amplitudes are already at wild-type levels by day 1 and that the homeostatic adjustment it studies completes within the first day post eclosion, so of the two sealed cohorts this is the one where a failure is least likely to be a developmental difference and most likely to be the model.

secondary.cohort: wild type, 0 days post eclosion (under 24 h), same genotype
secondary.why_it_is_secondary_and_what_that_costs: The frozen models carry no age parameter, so scoring them on an animal under 24 hours old tests a conjunction: that the model describes this synapse, and that wild-type ORN-to-PN short-term plasticity is already mature at eclosion. A failure here cannot be attributed between the two, and that is declared now rather than discovered afterwards. Its result is reported in full and does not enter the primary verdict.

excluded.Fig6D: paired-pulse ratios recorded from GABAergic multiglomerular local interneurons labelled by 449-QF. A different synapse class from the ORN-to-uniglomerular-PN edges ND-06's rule is scoped to. It stays sealed.
excluded.Fig3E_and_F: the train arrays at 1, 10, 20 and 60 Hz. A different observable rather than a different cohort, and the decisive test of the pinned recovery constant and of the additive-versus-multiplicative structure. It stays sealed and is the declared next experiment.
excluded.every_RNAi_array: a perturbation the frozen models have no parameter for. Sealed.

how_the_holdout_is_and_is_not_independen.same: the laboratory, the preparation, the stimulation protocol, the genotype, the measured quantity and the analysis code
how_the_holdout_is_and_is_not_independen.therefore: a cohort-generalisation test and a developmental extrapolation. Not an independent-laboratory test. Not a different observable. Not a perturbation.
how_the_holdout_is_and_is_not_independen.established_from: the paper's figure legends and methods, which are published prose and carry no reservation, cross-checked against the array shapes recorded in the sealed reservation manifest. No reserved value was read to establish any of it.

observation_model.protocol: twenty pairs at 0.2 Hz, simulated rather than assumed away, exactly as in the fit
observation_model.missing_data_rule: One paired-pulse ratio per animal. A non-finite entry excludes that animal from that interval and the count of exclusions is reported. Fixed here, before any value is opened.
observation_model.the_10_ms_measurement_differs_from_the_o: The methods state that at 10 ms the second amplitude was measured from the peak to the point of interception with the extrapolated first response. That is recorded again here, in advance, so that it can never be invoked afterwards as a reason to drop an interval a model failed on. All five intervals are scored on the same footing.

frozen_models.note: Copied from the fit artifact named in depends_on, not recomputed. The scorer re-derives each curve from the parameters below and refuses to run if the two disagree, which is how a change in the simulator between the freeze and the score is caught rather than absorbed.

selection.primary_rule: lowest weighted residual among eligible families
selection.secondary_rule: fewest parameters among the rest, ties by weighted residual
selection.why: two-timescale-facilitation-free carries the lowest weighted residual of the eligible families and is frozen as the primary. facilitation-depression is frozen alongside it as the secondary so an unseen cohort can adjudicate between them, which the fit set cannot.

primary.title: M4f: M4 with the fast facilitation constant fitted rather than pinned
primary.mechanism: The same two facilitating components as M4 over the same depleting resource, with the fast time constant fitted. It exists so that the decision to pin that constant is itself under test rather than assumed.
primary.structural_limits: Five free parameters against five cohort means leaves no residual degrees of freedom, so this family has no goodness-of-fit statistic and cannot be tested in sample at all. Its fast step and fast constant trade off along a ridge, so neither is separately determined by a curve whose shortest interval is 10 ms; what the data determine is the fast component's contribution at that one interval. Its facilitation is additive and has no ceiling of its own, but it multiplies a depleting resource and does not run away in a long train: over 112 pulses at 60 Hz it peaks near 1.4 times the first response at pulse four and falls to under three per cent of it by the end.

secondary.title: M1: release-probability facilitation over a depleting resource
secondary.mechanism: The standard two-state Markram-Tsodyks synapse. Residual calcium raises release probability for tens of milliseconds while the vesicle pool is depleted for hundreds, so a facilitating short interval and a depressing long one arise from one mechanism with two time constants.
secondary.structural_limits: The four parameters are in bijection with the four quantities a paired-pulse curve can identify, so nothing here is a fitted direction the observable cannot see. The ceiling of two is approached only as the resting utilisation goes to zero, where the response itself vanishes.

flat_null.why_it_is_here: A model that cannot beat a horizontal line on the holdout has not been tested by the holdout. This level is frozen with everything else so the comparison on unseen cohorts is between two predictions made in advance.

hypotheses.name: the frozen curve lands inside the unseen cohort's measurement error
hypotheses.statement: For the primary cohort, the primary frozen model's predicted ratio lies inside that cohort's two-sided 95 percent interval at every scorable interval except at most one.
hypotheses.criterion: at most one miss among the scorable intervals
hypotheses.why_one_miss_is_allowed: Five intervals scored at 95 percent confidence will produce about one excursion by chance even from a correct model. Demanding five of five would fail a correct model about a quarter of the time; allowing more than one would stop being a test. This tolerance is fixed now and is not adjustable afterwards.
hypotheses.degenerate_outcome_check: Any interval whose cohort 95 percent half-width exceeds 0.15 is recorded as NO VERDICT and drops out of the count, because a wide enough interval contains any prediction. If fewer than four intervals are scorable, A1 as a whole is NO VERDICT and no pass may be claimed from it.

hypotheses.name: the frozen curve beats a horizontal line
hypotheses.statement: For the primary cohort, the primary frozen model's weighted sum of squared residuals is at most half the flat null's weighted sum of squared residuals on the same cohort.
hypotheses.criterion: weighted residual ratio, model over null, at most 0.5
hypotheses.why_it_is_here: A1 alone can be passed by a model that predicts roughly the cohort mean at every interval, which is what the flat null does by construction. A2 is the guard against reading that as success, and both A1 and A2 must pass for the verdict to be a pass.
hypotheses.degenerate_outcome_check: If the flat null itself satisfies A1 on this cohort, A1 is declared uninformative for this run and the verdict rests on A2 alone. This is recorded rather than allowed to inflate the result.

hypotheses.name: the shape is right and not just the level
hypotheses.statement: For the primary cohort, the sign of the change between each adjacent pair of intervals in the frozen prediction agrees with the sign in the cohort means at three or more of the four adjacent pairs. A pair whose two cohort 95 percent intervals overlap counts as agreeing, because the data do not resolve its direction.
hypotheses.criterion: three or more of four adjacent comparisons agree
hypotheses.why_it_is_secondary: It is the criterion whose failure refuted ND-06 v0.1, so it must be scored; but the overlap allowance makes it weak on cohorts this size, and a weak criterion should not carry a verdict.

the_secondary_model_is_scored_and_awards.why_it_is_scored: The fit set cannot choose between the two eligible accounts of five means, so both were frozen and the unseen cohort is the only thing that can separate them. Scoring both is the point.
the_secondary_model_is_scored_and_awards.what_it_cannot_do: The secondary model's result does not create a pass. If the primary fails and the secondary passes, the recorded outcome is that the primary failed and that a differently-structured account did better on one cohort, which is a lead for the next contract and not a validation.
the_secondary_model_is_scored_and_awards.degenerate_outcome_check: If the two frozen models' predictions differ by less than 0.02 in ratio units at every interval, this holdout cannot separate them and that is recorded instead of a winner being declared.

expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.prediction: The primary is expected to pass A1 and A2 on the day-1 cohort, because the paper treats wild-type animals of these ages as equivalent controls and reports no wild-type difference across them, and because the frozen curve was fitted to the same quantity in the same preparation. The day-0 cohort is a genuine coin flip: it is the youngest animals and the least mature synapse.
expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.why_a_pass_is_expected_and_still_worth_r: An expected pass is a weak test, and saying so in advance is what stops it being reported as a strong one. What makes it worth running is that it is falsifiable, that the models are frozen with numbers written down, and that the alternative on offer is a project in which no dynamical model has ever been frozen and tested at all.
expected_outcome_stated_before_the_run.what_a_failure_would_mean: That not even cohort generalisation of the fitted observable holds, which would mean the fit is describing 22 particular animals rather than the synapse, and would leave the whole paired-pulse route to a dynamical tier closed rather than merely narrow.

acceptance.verdict_rule: PASS if and only if A1 and A2 both pass on the primary cohort. A3 and both secondary-cohort results are reported and do not enter the verdict.
acceptance.what_a_pass_would_establish: That a short-term-plasticity model for the ORN-to-PN synapse, frozen with its parameters written down before the data were seen, predicts an unseen cohort of the same observable in the same laboratory to within that cohort's measurement error, and does so better than a constant. That is the project's first passed dynamical validation, and it is worth a V1-limited tier on this observable only.
acceptance.what_a_pass_would_not_establish: Not V2 and nothing near it. It would not show the model predicts trains, latencies, absolute amplitudes, perturbations, another laboratory, another glomerulus or another synapse class. It would not make the fitted parameters measurements: the fit artifact records which of them this observable cannot determine, and those stay labelled. It would not reinstate the retired synaptic leg of the Stage 2 gate, which needs unitary waveforms this repository does not ship. The gate stays at v4 and 0 of 3.
acceptance.what_a_failure_would_establish: That the paired-pulse observable does not support a dynamical tier for this synapse on this connectome, and that the next attempt needs a different observable rather than a different model.
acceptance.no_refitting: No parameter may be changed on this outcome, and no successor may cite this test as evidence for its own values. That is the rule the 7 Hz failure and the paired-pulse failure were both recorded under and it holds identically here.
acceptance.no_criterion_may_be_restated: A1, A2, A3, their thresholds and all four degenerate-outcome checks are closed as of this commit.
acceptance.scored_once: The cohorts are opened once. This contract's values_opened flag is set on completion and the scorer refuses to run against a contract that already records them as opened.

the_next_experiment_whatever_happens_her.what: the sealed wild-type train arrays in rozenfeld2023-repo/Figure 3/Fig3E_and_F.mat, at 1, 10, 20 and 60 Hz over 32 to 112 pulses in 18 animals
the_next_experiment_whatever_happens_her.why_it_is_the_decisive_one: It is a different observable, not another cohort, and it attacks the weaknesses this exercise exposed. The frozen models pin a resource recovery constant that the paired-pulse protocol cannot measure at all; a 1 Hz train of 32 pulses measures it directly, and the two models predict steady states of 0.339 and 0.399 there. The additive and multiplicative accounts differ by a term that is invisible on a paired-pulse curve and compounds across a train: at 10 Hz they predict second-to-first ratios of 1.026 and 0.951 and put the peak at different pulses. And the fast facilitation component that the paired-pulse curve sees only at its 10 ms point is sampled repeatedly by a 60 Hz train, whose interval is 16.7 ms. An earlier version of this passage said the models would diverge in a long train and that a 60 Hz train would show it immediately. That was false, computed rather than asserted afterwards: the predictions are bounded near 1.4 and decay. The train experiment is a discrimination test, not an expected refutation.
the_next_experiment_whatever_happens_her.what_must_be_written_first: Its own contract, naming the file, the variables, the normalisation, the missing-data rule and the acceptance limits, committed before those arrays are opened. Nothing in this contract licenses opening them.

claim_boundary: One scoring pass over two sealed wild-type cohorts, against models frozen beforehand. It can award at most a V1-limited tier on the paired-pulse observable, it opens ten arrays and nothing else, and it leaves the trains, the perturbations, the raw traces and the entire Takagi corpus sealed.

the_artifact_records_a_verdict_that_does.why_it_does_not_stand: The artifact applied the registered verdict rule faithfully to the primary cohort. The primary cohort is not a holdout. Its five wild-type arrays are bit-identical to the five the model was fitted to, so A1 and A2 were scored against the training set and passing them means nothing. The artifact is immutable and is left exactly as written; this record supersedes its verdict field and any citation of it must cite this correction too.
the_artifact_records_a_verdict_that_does.why_not_simply_failed: The experiment did not fail; it was not run. A void cohort produces no evidence either way about the frozen models.

the_duplication.finding: rozenfeld2023-repo/Figure 3/Fig3J.mat stores the same five wild-type paired-pulse arrays as Fig3D.mat. Element-wise identical: same values, same order, same animal counts of 20, 21, 22, 22 and 22. The maximum absolute difference at every interval is exactly zero, and the digests of the stored element bytes match at all five.
the_duplication.what_it_means_about_the_paper: Nothing improper. The authors compared the 1-day-old cacRNAi cohort against the same wild-type reference they used for the 2-to-4-day comparison, and the repository ships that reference in both figure files. The RNAi arrays differ between the two files -- 28 animals in Fig3D against 22 in Fig3J -- so the perturbation cohorts are distinct. Only the wild-type control is shared.
the_duplication.how_it_was_discoverable_in_advance: From the published legends alone. Figure 3D gives wild-type n = 20 (10 ms), 21 (30 ms), 22 (100, 300, 1000 ms). Figure 3J gives wild-type n = 20 (10 ms), 21 (30 ms), 22 (100, 300, 1000 ms). Identical at every interval. The independence audit recorded both lines side by side in the fit contract and the coincidence was noticed and not acted on. That is the error: not a missing check, an unheeded one.
the_duplication.why_the_animal_counts_were_not_treated_a: Because Fig3H, the day-0 cohort, differs from the fit set at three of five intervals, which made the pattern look like ordinary cohort variation rather than reuse. That is a reason and not an excuse: identical counts at five independent intervals is not cohort variation, it is the same cohort.
the_duplication.the_structural_fix: flysim.reservations.duplicate_arrays compares the digests of the stored element bytes of named arrays across two files, decoding nothing, and flysim.stp_holdout now refuses to open any cohort that duplicates a spent one before a byte of payload is read. Run against this case it flags all five Fig3J arrays and clears all five Fig3H arrays. Equal stored bytes prove equal data, so a match is a refusal; unequal bytes prove nothing, so a clean result is a screen and not a certificate of independence.
the_duplication.the_third_instance_of_one_pattern: On 2026-09-09 the preparation was inferred from a plotting label instead of read from the methods. Earlier on 2026-09-10 a join size was inferred from a file's row count instead of measured on its column. Now a cohort's independence was inferred from a figure legend's prose instead of checked against its own numbers. All three were cheap to check, none was checked, and all three unchecked readings favoured the project. The two automated guards added since -- the byte-level worktree audit and this duplicate-array check -- address the mechanism, not the habit.

what_the_genuine_cohort_returned.cohort: wild type, 0 days post eclosion (under 24 h), same genotype
what_the_genuine_cohort_returned.status: a real unseen cohort: its arrays differ from the fit set at every interval and its animal counts differ at three of five
what_the_genuine_cohort_returned.registered_role: secondary, declared in advance not to enter the verdict

A1.note: Only 3 of 5 intervals are scorable under the registered half-width limit of 0.15, below the registered minimum of 4.
A1.reading: The 10 ms and 30 ms cohorts have 95 percent half-widths of about 0.19 and 0.17 against the registered 0.15 limit, so three of five intervals are scorable and the registered minimum is four. The frozen prediction does in fact lie inside all five intervals, but the registered power check forbids reading that as a pass, and it forbids it for the right reason: an interval that wide would contain a great many wrong predictions too.

A2.reading: This is the one substantive registered result the run produced. On 21 animals the frozen model had never seen, its weighted residual is about 26 times smaller than a frozen constant's, against a registered limit of 2 times. A2 does not require narrow intervals -- it asks whether the curve tracks the means better than a horizontal line -- so the power problem that voided A1 does not void this.

A3.reading: All four adjacent directions agree. Weak, because the overlap allowance makes it easy on cohorts this size, and the flat null also passes it.

the_secondary_model_on_the_same_cohort.reading: The four-parameter single-facilitation model does marginally better than the five-parameter two-timescale one on this cohort: weighted residuals of 1.279 against 1.493. The difference is far too small to separate them and it points the opposite way from the fit set, where the two-timescale family was better by a factor of hundreds. So the question the two frozen models were meant to adjudicate is not adjudicated, and the honest statement is that one unseen cohort of this size cannot tell them apart.

what_the_genuine_cohort_returned.what_this_cohort_cannot_support: A pass of the experiment. It was registered as secondary and declared in advance not to enter the verdict, and promoting it now because the primary turned out void would be exactly the criterion-restatement this contract forbids in its own acceptance section.

D1.on_the_genuine_cohort: two of five dropped for width, which is what turned A1 into NO VERDICT there

D2.reading: the constant failed A1, so A1 would have carried information had the cohort been real

D3.this_is_the_check_that_caught_it: It was written to detect a holdout whose means sit within one fit-set standard error of the fit set, on the reasoning that such a cohort is a replication rather than a test. What it found was stronger than that: differences of exactly 0.0000 at all five intervals. A difference of exactly zero is not a replication, it is the same data, and the check's recorded consequence -- record the pass as a replication -- is too weak for what it found. Its wording is corrected in the reissue.

D4.reading: The two frozen curves differ by up to 0.075 at 100 ms, above the registered 0.02 limit, so a cohort of adequate power could have separated them. The genuine cohort's 100 ms half-width is 0.12, which is not adequate power.

execution_record.no_refitting: Nothing was refitted on this outcome. The frozen parameters in this contract and in short-term-plasticity-v0.2 are unchanged, and no successor may cite either cohort as evidence for its values. Fig3H is now spent; Fig3J was never anything but the fit set.
execution_record.what_remains_unspent: The wild-type train arrays of rozenfeld2023-repo/Figure 3/Fig3E_and_F.mat, at 1, 10, 20 and 60 Hz over 32 to 112 pulses in 18 animals. After this run they are the only unspent wild-type ORN-to-PN holdout in the corpus, which raises rather than lowers the standard for the contract that opens them.
